【53】**Abdominal Mass， Generalized**

【54】As the physician examines the abdomen， how can he or she recall all of the causes of a mass or swelling? The physician should consider the possibilities for the mass's composi-tion. It may be air， in which case the physician would think of air in the peritoneum with rupture of a viscus， particu-larly a peptic ulcer， or it may be air in the intestinal tract from focal or generalized distention， in which case the phy-sician would recall gastric dilatation， intestinal obstruction related to numerous causes ， or paralytic ileus. The mass may be fluid， in which case the physician would recall fluid in the abdominal wall (anasarca)， the perito-neum  and its various causes， and fluid(urine\] accumulation in the bladder or intestine or cysts of other abdominal organs. The lWatter brings to mind ovar-ian， pancreatic， and omental cysts. The mass may be blood in the peritoneal wall， the peritoneum， or any of the organ systems of the abdomen. The mass may be a solid inor-ganic substance， such as the fecal accumulation in celiac disease and Hirschsprung disease. Finally， the mass may be a hypertrophy， swelling， or neoplasm of any one of the organs or tissues in the abdomen.

【55】This is where anatomy comes in. In the abdominal wall， there may be an accumulation of fat (obesity). The liver may be enlarged by neoplasm or obstruction of its vascular supply (e.g.， Budd-Chiari syndrome or cardiac cirrhosis) or by obstruction of the biliary tree with neo-plasms or biliary cirrhosis. The spleen may become mas-sively enlarged by hypertrophy， hyperplasia in Gaucher disease， infiltration of cells in chronic myelogenous leuke-mia and myeloid metaplasia， or by inflammation in kala azar. The kidney rarely enlarges to the point at which it causes a generalized abdominal swelling in hydronephro-sis， but a Wilms tumor or carcinoma may occasionally become extremely large.

【56】The bladder， as mentioned above， may be enlarged sufficiently to present a generalized abdominal swell-ing when it becomes obstructed， but a neoplasm of the bladder will not present as a huge mass. The uterus pres-ents as a generalized abdominal mass in late stages of pregnancy， but ovarian cysts should be first considered in huge masses arising from the female genital tract. Pancreatic cysts and pseudocysts are possible causes of a generalized abdominal swelling， although they are usu-ally localized to the right upper quadrant (RUQ) or epi-gastrium. It would be unusual for an aortic aneurysm to grow to a size sufficient to cause a generalized abdominal mass， but it is frequently mentioned in differential diag-nosis texts.

The above method is one method of developing a dif-ferential diagnosis of generalized abdominal swelling or|删除1换行|mass. Relying solely on anatomy and cross-indexing the various structures with the mnemonic MINT is another. This mnemonic is suggested as an exercise for the reader. Take each organ system as a tract. Thus， the gastrointes-tinal (GI) tract presents most commonly with a diffuse swelling in intestinal obstruction and paralytic ileus； the biliary tract and pancreas with hepatitis， neoplasms， and pancreatic pseudocysts. The urinary tract presents with a diffuse “mass" in bladder neck obstruction. The female genital tract may be the cause of a huge abdominal mass in ovarian cysts， neoplasms， and pregnancy. Apply the same technique to the spleen and abdominal wall to complete the picture.

【58】There are， in addition， certain conditions that cause abdominal swelling that is more apparent than real. Lumbar lordosis causes abdominal protuberance， as does visceroptosis. A huge ventral hernia or diastasis recti may mimic an abdominal swelling. Psychogenic protrusion of the belly by straining is another cause.

【59】**Approach to the Diagnosis**

【60】What can be done to work up a diffuse abdominal swell-ing? It is important to catheterize the bladder if there is any question that this may be the cause. A flat plate of the abdomen and lateral decubiti and upright films will help in diagnosing intestinal obstruction， a ruptured viscus， or peritoneal fluid. A pregnancy test must be done in women of childbearing age. If pregnancy or ovarian cysts can be definitively excluded by ultrasonography， then a computed tomography (CT) scan or diagnostic peritoneal tap may be helpful in the diagnosis

【34】**5.6 Dyslexia and the primary progressive aphasias**

【35】**Disorders of understanding and pronouncing written words are called peripheral or central dyslexia. Depending on etiology and localization， lesions of the medial temporal gyrus， or supramarginal parietal gyrus in the left hemisphere are associated with “deep dyslexia”or “phonological dyslexia，” whereas lesions of the angular gyrus and ventral anterior temporal lobe are referred to as “sur-face dyslexia." Both kinds of dyslexia belong to the group of central dyslexia.**

【36】**Patients with surface dyslexia try to pronounce words by grapheme-phoneme correspondence rules and are therefore slow in reading and have problems espe-cially in producing irregularly spoken words when reading them. Reading speed decreases with increasing word length since they are unable to read automati-cally. Therefore they use grapheme-phoneme correspondence rules to come up with a phonological interpretation of the specific letter combination (the word they are reading) that fits a possible semantic meaning of the word. Patients with deep dyslexia (the opposite pattern of impairment) are unable to read pseu-dowords because their deficit concerns the knowledge about the grapheme-phoneme correspondence rules. They read automatically， without using the rules， by their extensive knowledge of the words. Automatic processing depends on how often one has done a specific task. Therefore patients with deep dys-lexia have problems reading words they have not encountered often during their life (e.g.， foreign words) or that carry an abstract meaning (infrequently read). Some patients with deep dyslexia not only lose the grapheme-phoneme corre-spondence rules but also suffer from problems accessing the semantic meaning of the words. As these patients read based on automatic phonological knowl-edge， the impairment is often called phonological dyslexia instead of deep dys-lexia. Because such patients do not understand the words they are reading， they have problems with ambiguous interpretation of syllables and words (the German words “Baum'artand“Bau’markt" are good examples of needing to know the meaning of the words to come up with a correct phonological interpretation).**

【37】**Compared to the other clinical syndromes of PPAs surface dyslexia is a dis-tinctive sign of SD， whereas nfPPA and lPPA patients seem to suffer more often from phonological dyslexia. Chare et al. (2014) analyzed the different impairments of the three PPAs and found that， apart from the specific aphasic and dysarthric symptoms， the frequency of surface dyslexia differed between the groups. Surface dyslexia was much more common in SD patients. Matias-Guiu et al. (2017) compared the three different clinical syndromes of PPA for their language and reading behavior. All three groups were impaired in the word fluency tasks， however， the nfPPA group more in phonological word flu-ency than in categorial and the SD group more in categorial than in phonologi-cal word fluency. Patients with lPPA were severely impaired in sentence repetition. In addition， the other groups also showed some but clearly less pro-blems in repetition compared to the healthy control group. The nfPPA group suffered from a severe spelling deficit， the SD group suffered from deficits in all semantic tasks and in picture naming. Concerning reading， Matias-Guiu et al. (2017) used regular words， foreign words and words without stress marks， and nonwords as task items. All three groups were able to read regular words and all three groups had problems reading foreign language words . The SD group could perfectly read pronounceable nonwords， whereas the two other groups were impaired in this task. However， the SD group had considerable problems reading irregular wor

【2】**6.6 Treatment of behavioral frontal temporal dementia**

【3】**The German guidelines for dementia state that there is currentlyno evidence-based pharmacological treatments of FTD. Thus the major target for pharmacological intervention is to reduce the behavioral symptoms and not to treat the disease. Memantine and cholinesterase inhibitors have not demonstrated clinically significant efficacy in treating FTD patients and may also hasten cognitive decline or worsen behavioral symptoms. As FTD patients do not seem to suffer from a cholinergic deficit， one would also not expect an improvement.**

【4】**There is limited evidence that selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors(SSRIs) may reduce impulsivity， irritability， disinhibition， and changes in eat-ing behavior . For example， in a small RCT， paroxetine reduced symptoms severity scored with the NPI. However， a study using the same drug with higher dosage showed no effect at all. Quite the contrary high-er dosage of paroxetine seemed to induce cognitive impairments. The outcome differences of these studies are unclear. It is possible that higher dosage of par-oxetine lead to an overstimulation of the serotonergic system. On the other hand the patients of the second study were somewhat later in their disease pro-gression and pharmacological treatment may no longer have been effective. Similar effects have been documented for citalopram， which is also an (newer) SSRI. There are also some case studies showing an effect for sertraline.**

【13】**6.7 Summary**

【14】Decrease of social contacts， emotional impoverishment， early decrease of criti-cism， and lack of insight can be defined as cardinal symptoms of the behav-ioral variant of FTD. On a behavioral level， conspicuousSbehavior. disinhibition in social interaction， loss of interest (e.g.， in self-care)， and risky decision making characterize the disease. bvFTD is caused by different neuro-pathological pathways but may be related to focused loss of two specific cells types of the brain： the von Economo and the fork cells (discussed later).

【15】**Neuropsychological testing of patients with bvFTD should encompass prefrontal lobe functions sensitive tests (e.g.， working memory and flexibility of the TAP)， the RMET， Picture arrangement of the WIE， and the NPI answered by close friends or relatives. Tests for affective empathy and the object alternation task are especially sensitive in the early stages of bvFTD. Patients with bvFTD exhibit declined performance on tests assessing cogni-tive empathy and executive functions but not so much in the very early phase of their disease process. Standardneuropsychological tests such as the CERAD-NAB and the DemTect are not effective for a differential diagnosis of bvFTD.**

【16】Apart from the core set of tests， the neuropsychological differential diag-nosis of bvFTD should include at least two social perception or understand-ing tasks and the“RMET” has proven to be sensitive and of prognostic value. Patients with bvFTD suffer from emotion recognition deficits and these concern negative emotions more than positive emotions. On a cognitive level the object alternation (termed flexibility) task of the TAP should be used for the assessment. If there is any indication for bvFTD， the NPI should be answered by a relative of the patient. Changes in eating behavior and in irritability， disinhibition， and distraction are of major interest. Moreover the clinical observation should look for signs of prehension behavior and the anamnesis and increasing tension in the relationship not only related to increase irritability but also to a loss of affective empathy.

【17】**The neuroradiological assessment of the patients might show atrophy in the insular and the anterior cingulate and ventromedial prefrontal cortex； however， the diagnosis cannot be based on MRI scanning. There may be an increase level of total tau and phosphor-tau in bvFTD patients. Unfortunately this is not always the case. Therefore the diagnosis primarily depends on the clinical assessment.**

**Up to now there is no specific treatment for bvFTD neither on a func-tional nor on a pharmacological level. Serotonergic modulation might have the potential for symptom modulation (reducing disinhibition in the patients)， but there is no large-scale RCT to show that on a high level of evidence. The German guidelines for dementia argue for risperidone to reduce the behavioral impairments in bvFTD. In any case relatives of bvFTD should be offered professional education on how to deal with their affected family|删除1换行|members， because their behavior leads to severe losses of quality of live and often poses the question how to respond correctly. 【32】**We started this section with the question whether there are single CERAD-NAB subtest-based cut-off scores that can be used for the differen-tial diagnosis between different neurodegenerative diseases. Our analysis showed that there are no single test scores providing such information. We then tried to define patterns of deficit that can be assessed by the combina-tion of CERAD-NAB test scores and asked if such combinations are more helpful for the purpose of differential diagnosis. We found that the combina-tion of tests seems to improve the prospect for differential diagnosis. Some of these patterns show moderate correlations with CSF biomarkers and this holds especially true for the combination of the memory tasks. On the other hand， it also became clear that a simple combination of tests stemming from the same domain (e.g.， all concerning memory or language functions) still does not offer a complete solution for the problem. We concluded that the best solution is the combination of patterns of tests： being impaired in one domain but unimpaired in other domains. This leads to the consequence that the clinical knowledge about the meaning of the pattern is what counts.**

【1】In addition， the reliability of self-report is very uncertain if someone is ex-periencing psychotic symptoms. The stigma of mental illness and the fear of psychiatric treatment may lead to underreporting symptoms. Consequently， it is often helpful to gather data from collateral sources， such as close friends or relatives， employers， or other professionals， to specify both the timing and severity of symptoms. Assessment may be further complicated by co-occurring conditions (medical， psychiatric， and substance problems). Being able to dif-ferentiate age-appropriate behaviors from the symptoms of bipolarity is espe-cially important when dealing with children. Knowledge of diagnostic specifiers and their pharmacological implications is key to successful assessment and will greatly improve the treatment of this lifelong disorder. Furthermore， research is limited on the effects that race/ethnicity， gender， and/or age may have on stan-dardized screening measures and assessment tools. Appreciating these cultural differences and understanding any bias that may exist is essential to decreasing disparities in diagnosis and treatment.

【2】**Assessment Instruments**

【3】Depression When assessing depressive symptoms in bipolar disorder， many rating scales and tools can be useful. The Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) is a simple， self-administered screening measure of depression that was developed and studied in primary care settings. It generally takes under 10 minutes to complete. The PHQ-9 combines 8 questions related to DSM-IV depression diag-nostic criteria  along with 1 question about suicidal ideation， which are summed to produce a total score. Also， an additional question on functional status (which is not scored) is provided to help with treatment planning. Individ-uals rate their problems/feelings over the “past 2 weeks”on a 4-point scale (from0 = not at all to 3 = nearly every day) with total scores ranging from 0 to 27. When total score is under 5， depression severity is seen as none to minimal. Totals ranging from 5， 10，15， and 20 represent thresholds for mild， moderate， moder-ately severe， and severe depression， respectively .

【4】The PHQ-9 has excellent internal consistency and strong psychometrics in-cluding criterion and convergent validity. At the recommended cutoff score of 10or higher， the PHQ-9 has a sensitivity of 88% and specificity of 88% for identi-fying patients with a major depressive episode . Also， in comparison to 9 other measures of depression， the PHQ had a positive predictive value of 7.1 versus 2.9， meaning that the PHQ had a higher chance of catching major depression . It demon-strated good sensitivity (89.5%) and specificity (77.5%) at a recommended cut-off of 11 or above in adolescents， which was similar to adult studies . The PHQ was able to detect major and minor depression among geriatric primary care patients  and effective in ethnic and racially diverse patients .

The CGI-BP can measure illness phases (e.g.， manic， depressive， and total illness) as well as evaluate treatment response in bipolar illness (both acute and long-term pre-vention). 【18】**Emergency Considerations**

【19】Assessing and managing suicide risk is one of the most important compo-nents of clinical practice， especially when treating individuals with bipolar and related disorders. Having a Bipolar and Related Disorder is a risk factor for both suicide attempts and the primary cause of premature death from suicide . A large epidemiological study by Simon， Hunkeler， Fireman， Lee， & Savarino (2007) showed among indi-viduals treated for bipolar disorders； 1 per 1，000 person-years die by suicide；5.6 per 1，000 person-years attempt suicide leading to hospitalization and almost 14% attempt suicide not leading to hospitalization. These numbers were echoed in World Mental Health Survey Initiative， which showed that1 in 4 individuals with BP-I and 1 in 5 individuals with BP-II have a history of suicide attempts . Furthermore， when differenti-ating between individuals with bipolar II disorder and those with bipolar I disorder or unipolar depression the major clinical feature is the risk of suicide. For both adults and adolescents， having a bipo-lar disorder is a predictive factor for completed suicide， and early illness onset is a risk factor for suicidal behavior .

【20】In some situations， people experiencing severe emotional distress may constitute a danger to themselves or others. Suicidal thinking is part of the diagnostic criteria for a major depressive episode. In some major depressive episodes， and in most manic episodes， some degree of psychosis is present. In these situations， practitioners must attend to issues about the client’s safety and secure whatever level of supervision and treatment is necessary. A comprehen-sive suicide risk assessment will help identify the major risk factors for suicidal behavior. Suicidal and emotionally distressed individuals are often not reliable sources for self-report. This can impede risk assessment and heighten the need to seek information from others including family and friends. 【22】Cultural Considerations

【23】Cultural variations impact symptom expression and， therefore， they can af-fect the diagnostic process. Addressing cross-cultural and gender differences is paramount when treating individuals who suffer from bipolar disorder. Cultural attitudes also influence whether individuals will seek help and which treatment approaches may be most effective. Multiple studies have found that individuals from Hispanic and Asian backgrounds are more likely to report physical ailments and less likely to report emotional symptoms when suf-fering from mental illness. In many cultures， the stigma surrounding mental illness is very strong， and the pressure “not to shame the family”often leads to underreporting symptoms. Cultural sensitivity education and training for English-speaking practitioners are important aspects of competent mental health practice.

【24】In keeping with findings from the previous National Comorbity Survey (NCS) data from the National Comorbidity Survey Replication (NCS-R) _·_ showed thatdisadvantaged ethnic groups have a lower lifetime risk for psychiatric disorders. However， new data emerged revealing that this lower risk emerges at a very young age (typically before age 10)， and although they have a lower lifetime risk，they are more likely to be persistently ill. The lower prevalence for non-Hispanic Blacks and Hispanics over non-Hispanic whites held true for all mood disorders(including depression) except for the lifetime prevalence of bipolar and related disorders (4.9%， 4.3%， and 3.2%， respectively) .

【25】Another caution relates to the tendency for minority group members to re-ceive more serious or more stigmatized psychiatric labels. For example， there is some evidence that Caucasians are more likely to be diagnosed with Bipolar I Disorder， while minority clients with the same symptom presentation are diag-nosed with schizophrenic disorders . Also， African Americans with bipolar disorder tend to present with more severe psychotic symptoms and be more likely prescribed antipsychotics . Many feel the symptom expression of bipolarity in African Ameri-cans may be misconstrued. For example， Gonzalez et al.， (2010) uses the example of how a persecutory delusion might be assessed as motivated by anxiety rather than as a symptom of psychosis. A study of data from the National Epidemiologic Survey on Alcohol and Related Conditions (NESARC； 2001-2002) suggest that clinician biases rather than fundamental racial/ethnic differences in symptom pre-sentation are responsible for the misdiagnosis of bipolar disorders .

【13】**2.8.4 Prediction of conversion with the help of specific memory processes**

**Aforesaid， the primacy and the recency proportion testing wordlist leamning is a specific sign for an amnestic syndrome of the hippocampal type and that changes in these proportions supplement information about the cause for mem-ory impairment to classical consolidation testing. A small number of studies analyzed the possibility to predict the conversion of patients with MCI to AD with the help of their performance in the primacy and recency proportion. Using the CVLT， Cunha et al. (2012) first showed that MCI and AD showed a similar impairment in the primacy proportion of wordlist reproduction. This was not the case for the recency part of the wordlist， where MCI and healthy controls produced a similar percent of words and only AD patients showed a reduced performance. Cunha et al. (2012) followed the patients for 4 years and analyzed the possibility to predict the conversion of the MCI patients to AD by the help of the primacy proportion. The primacy regional score identi-fied 78% of MCI patients who progressed to AD (sensitivity) and 60% of the|删除1换行|nonconverters (specificity). With 70% correct prediction the primacy score was moderately effective in the prognosis of MCI patients converting to AD.**

**Performing false alarms during recognition testing is another specific fea-ture of AD and is related to a progressive decline of hippocampal-based rec-ollection anda smaller impairment in recognition by familiarity and correlating with biomarkers like tau and beta-amyloid (1-42). There is at least one small study that used visualrecognition performance to predict clinical progression. DDiiddiicc eett aall. ((22001133)) used a delayed matching tto san test (DMS48) in patients with amnestic MCI and followed these patients for up to 6 years. In this study， patients studied 48 colored paired picture draw-ings and had to judge whether the number of colors in these drawings was less than or greater than three. After a delay period filled with a 2-minute phonemic fluency task， the original picture paired with a similar or a dissimi-lar picture was presented again， and the patients had to rate which picture had been presented before. A second recognition trial took place 1 hour later. In the recognition trials of the DMS48 only two items are shown at a time and an incorrect item is always paired with a correct item. In other words， there are no pairs without a correct item. These two features distinguish the DMS48 test from the picture recognition test， which we used in our study. After 6 years， 15 patients (58%) of the  study met the criteria for AD. At baseline， converters differed from nonconverters only in scores assessing memory， including tasks asses-sing anterograde memory and retrograde semantic memory. There were no differences between converters and nonconverters on the MMSE， activities|删除1换行|of daily living， memory complaints， a depression scale score and tests evalu-ating executive functions， naming， visuoperceptive and visuospatial skills. Performance on the DMS48 predicted conversion to AD with a sensitivity of80% and a specificity of 90.9%， however， delayed recall of text reproduction of the WMS IV showed， in absolute terms， a slightly higher accuracy. The combination of the results from text reproduction and the DSM48 revealed a specificity and a sensitivity of 100%. Thus picture recognition and verbal memory together lead to an optimal classification of the patients.**

【16】**De Simone， Perri， Fadda， Caltagirone， and Carlesimo (2019) directly com-pared the power of delayed recall and false positives in recognition memory during wordlist learning to predict the conversion to dementia over the course of 3 years. Stable MCI patients showed impaired free recall but improved more than healthy controls during recognition testing. Recognition perfor-mance correctly classified patients who showed a converting or a stable MCI and the classification was more accurate than the classification based on free recall. The ability to discriminate between hits and distractors was an espe-cially useful diagnostic tool for predicting progression to AD dementia from the prodromal stage of MCI. After 3 years， only about 30% of patients with false positives in recognition memory still had MCIs， whereas above 70% of the patients without false positives in recognition did not convert to dementia.**

【17】**These small-scale studies seem to contradict the results of Mistridis et al.(2015) who found that the discrimination index of the CERAD-NAB was not very effective in predicting the conversion of the patients. However， the rec-ognition subtests of the CERAD-NAB (and of most of the clinical wordlist learning tests) are much easier to perform than the delayed free recall sub-test. The relative easier task load of recognition may lead to ceiling effects for recognition performance in participants with mild memory impairments but， at the same time， they may already show impaired performance in free recall tasks (which is prognostically meaningful but unspecific for AD). In the small-scale studies by De Simone et al. (2019) and Didic et al. (2013) the recognition task was more difficult than the CERAD-NAB recognition task. Therefore the predictive power of recognition might have been higher.**

【18】**Another problem that is related to this issue is that recognition memory tests do not always distinguish between false positives and misses (e.g.， the CERAD-NAB) and most tests that do distinguish between false positives and misses are verbal learning tests. It is well known that words do not produce strong familiar-ity effects. More recent and more experimental recognition testing includes visual distractors that invite patients to rely more on familiarity judgments than on words. These paradigms have shown that AD patients produce many false positive errors as a response to such distractors. Therefore testing of AD patients should include recognition measures with highly prototypical pictures.**

**Without taking the more recent study results regarding the specific mem-ory impairments in AD into account， it is unlikely that a prediction regarding the development of the disease can reach higher levels of sensitivity and specificity with neuropsychological measures alone. Future studies should|删除1换行|try to integrate recognition tasks with a similar difficulty as delayed free recall. It is highly probable that the power to predict conversion based on recognition performance will then increase.**

【20】**2.8.5 Problems for predicting conversion to dementia using neuropsychological test results**

【21】**Reul， Lohmann， Wiendl， Duning， and Johnen (2017) analyzed whether the CERAD-NAB along with other tests， that is， a core test battery for dementia as proposed earlier， was able to discriminate between early stage AD and bvFTD patients. They followed 43 patients who later received a clinically verified AD diagnosis and 26 patients who later received a clini-cally verified bvFTD diagnosis. Verbal recall， figure copy and imitation of face postures and limb gestures contributed to the differential diagnosis. Seventy-seven percent of the bvFTD patients and 90% of the AD patients could be classified correctly using these four test variables. Attention testing(TMT-A)， executive function performance and social cognition， however， did not distinguish between the patient groups. Unfortunately the ability to differentially predict conversion to AD specifically (as opposed to FTD or vascular dementia) using neuropsychological test results has not been tested in larger patient groups and has yet to be demonstrated.**

【22】**2.8.6 A note on prediction from mild cognitive impairment to dementia based on biomarkers**

参考段删除-1:<u>In a study conducted by Caminiti et al. (2018)， FDG-PET with SPM classification together with additional post hoc postprocessing algorithms improved the correct</u>|删除换行|classification of pure neuropsychological investigations from 32 to 35 of the 39patients who converted to AD. FDG-PET was， however， not more accurate than CSF markers， that is， compared with phosphor-tau/beta-amyloid (1-42) or the total tau/beta-amyloid ratio. Nevertheless， in this study， the sensitivity of FDG-PET along with specific post hoc postprocessing algorithms increased the sensitiv-ity from 82% to 90% (compared with a neuropsychological-based prediction). Unfortunately the specific tests used for the neuropsychological assessment are not described in the methods section of the study. On a global level， the accuracy of a CSF biomarker-based prognosis for AD (vs other kinds of dementia) is around 80% (depending on the length of the follow-up).**

【24】**Unfortunately the new beta-amyloid PET tracers are not better predictors than CSF analysis . A recent longitudinal study by van Maurik et al. (2017) showed that for patients with MCI， even the combination of different biomar-kers and a MMSE score of 24 increased the prognosis of converting to demen-tia after 3 years to maximum 89% (with two impaired MRI features and two impaired CSF results)， which is surprisingly low considering that the patients already exhibited a MMSE score of 24. Furthermore the 1-year conversion rate was below 26%. Without any abnormalities in the CSF， the risk of con-verting to dementia for patients with an MMSE score of 24 decreased to 6%. Including patients with an MMSE score of less than 29 (i.e.， patients with only subtle cognitive impairments) reduced the highest conversion prediction with two impaired biomarkers to 16% after 1 year and to 64% for a 3-year time frame. This is not much higher than the standard prediction made without incorporating biomarkers and based solely on the knowledge that a patient suf-fers from MCI (about a 10% conversion ratio per year). In general， predictions based on MRI features were less precise than predictions based on CSF values. On a more global level， the study by van Maurik et al. (2017) showed that even the best clinically used biomarkers are far from perfect when it comes to predicting conversion to dementia.**

【26】**2.8.7 Summarv**

Statistically significant differences between groups of patients who will show cognitive decline or convert to dementia can be shown up to 10 years|删除1换行|before the disease manifests. The majority of the studies identified that delayed free recall is the most sensitive parameter for detecting future cogni-tive decline， but this depends on the difficulty of the memory test that is used. A significant difference between groups is not enough to predict decline in single patients， however. When making predictions for single patients， the current memory loss of the patient should be evident in several different tests， not only in one test， even if this test offers various results (for learning， delayed free recall， recognition). If the functional loss is low， the chance of recovering from MCI is almost the same as the risk of declining. If the loss is high， the risk of declining increases. For the CERAD-NAB， it can be stated that remembering less than 15 words during the three learning trials increases the risk for a further decline up to 50% during the next 3years (in patients older than 74 years).**

【28】Most of the studies on predicting cognitive decline or converting to AD used classical neuropsychological tests. There is a paucity of studies that focus on more AD-specific and AD-characteristic memory impairments such as the primacy index， paired associate learning and false positives in recogni-tion. Studies using such tests might lead to an improved predictive power of neuropsychological testing.

【30】**Discussing the results of the neuropsychological examination concern-ing the prognosis with patients is centered around the term “risk." It is very important to emphasize that a risk concerns something that might happen and not something that will necessarily happen. Otherwise， the patient might think he or she will develop a dementia either way， which could lead to depressive mood and a sharp reduction of quality of life. Such an inevitable interpretation of the term risk， however， is wrong. Therefore the meaning of an increased risk should be explicitly communi-cated. Furthermore several examples should be provided to the patients to ameliorate the understanding of the difference between increased risk and a causal consequence.**

【31】**2.9Is a treatment of Alzheimer’s disease and mild cognitive impairment effective and therefore necessary?**

【32】**2.9.1Lifestyle and pharmacological interventions in mild cognitive impairment patients and the conversion to Alzheimer’s disease**

【33】**Not only among the general public but also in the world of neurologists， psy-chiatrists， and psychologists， the diagnosis of dementia is often conceptual-ized as a disease that cannot be treated. Summarizing the results regarding**

【34】**MCI treatment， the German guideline for dementia states that there is no evi-dence for an effective pharmacological or nonpharmacological treatment to reduce the risk of conversion toward dementia. This is a strong statement， that is， on the one hand， correct because there are no randomized controlled trials that show such a risk reduction. On the other hand， there are now many indications that changing one’s lifestyle and enhancing somatic and mental fitness can delay the progression of cognitive decline . Epidemiological studies have shown that there are at least some protective factors that may delay the development of AD. One of the most important factors is education . People that have achieved higher levels of education seem to be able to compensate for the progression of the disease for a longer period of time and can therefore maintain independence. It is， however， not entirely clear what this relationship between education and disease progres-sion really implies. One interpretation is that in patients with higher educa-tion deterioration also start from a higher level， therefore the disease progression takes longer to reach such a state of mental decline where the severity corresponds to a dementia syndrome. The other interpretation is that higher education implies higher neuronal reserve capacities of the brain. This would mean that the neuronal plasticity in these patients is higher than in patients with less education (not unlike an epigenetic triggering of neuronal regeneration). In this case， education would have a direct impact on neurode-generation and slow its progression.**

【35】**There are many studies that found an impact of education on the prevalence of dementia. The study found that the twin， who became affected later， performed a more complex job decades before the dementia was diag-nosed. 【37】**5Differential Diagnosis of Toxic Exposure**

【38】**_Alice Armstrong_**

【39】**DEFINING TOXIC ENCEPHALOPATHY**

【40】**Encephalopathy，broadly speaking， is any disease of the brain. There are multiple types of encephalopathy， with etiologies ranging from direct effects (e.g.， viral) to indirect effects of medical disease (e.g.， cardiac and hepatic systems). Encephalopathy from toxin exposure does not， however， have a unificd， well-defined clinical presentation. Presentation depends on the toxin， the dose， the duration， and the route of adminis-tration. Standard textbooks of internal medicine or neurology often do not provide a section on “toxic”encephalopathy， and frequently fail to include individual toxins as possible etiologies for encephalitis， If a toxic exposure is a consideration in a differential diagnosis，occupational medicine literature is often the best resource.**

【41】**The term toxic encephalopathy represents a broad scope of cerehral effects cauised by “toxic"doses from many classes of substances (metals， solvents， pesticides， and other chemicals). Acute toxic encephalopathy has a sudden onset following a new exposure， and often will resolve within hours to days of onset， depending on toxin and dose. A careful history of occupation and personal pastimes will usually identify expo-sure to a causative toxin during the period just before onset. Chronic encephalopathy， often less dramatic in presentation， can represent permanent deficits of insidious damage to the central nervous system. At times， the patient will provide a history of multiple， previously undiag-nosed episodes of mild acute encephalopathy， sometimes over years of exposure.**

【42】**Each class of toxic substance may produce a cluster of neurochemi-cal， anatomical， and behavioral effects that may not be limited to the nervous system， and individual substances within each class vary in their toxicity. The solvent toluene， for example， has a more potent toxic effect than many other aromatic hydrocarbons. Thus each suspected“toxic encephalopathy” must be evaluated against a pattern based on the literature of previous clinical experience with the suspected toxin.**

【43】**This chapter identifies the sources of encephalopathy reported from toxic exposures， as well as the differential diagnostic considerations of other encephalopathic etiologies or psychiatric disorders. As the response to toxic exposure aiso varies markedly among individuals， a major resource for the diagnosis of toxic encephalopathy is a neuropsycholog ical evaluation. This chapter also provides suggestions for the selection of and collaboration with a neuropsychologist.**

【44】**Magnitude of the Problem**

【45】**It is estimated that more than nine million individuals contact neuro-toxins in the workplace . No reliable source has been located to esti-mate the number of workers who become encephalopathic from toxins. Clinically， there is a sense that mild toxic encephalopathy is relatively common and underreported.**

【46】**Populations at Risk**

【47】**White， Feldman， and Proctor (1992) provide a list of industries and processes that frequently utilize neurotoxins. Even if the patient does not initially report toxin-related complaints， employment in one in these occupations or processes， along with presentation of related symp-toms， should raise the consideration of toxin exposure in the differen-tial diagnosis. **

【48】**Non-occupational Risk Factors**

【49】**In addition to risks identificd in the factors for consideration of differ-ential diagnosis， other factors include avocational interests (hobbies， crafts)， ambient environmental exposures， and the synergistic effects of chemicals (e.g.， solvent mixtures， or worklife-personal life interactions such as mild occupational exposure simultaneously with drug abuse， alcohol abuse， and possibly including some nutrients).**

【52】**CLNICALPRESENTATION**

【53】**Acute Exposure**

**The general symptoms of acute encephalopathy from moderate to high toxin exposure are similar to other types of encephalopathy： involve-ment of the parenchymal brain tissue is indicated by alterations in the state of consciousness. In the majority of cases， altered sensorium is the only neurolgic finding. The diagnosis of acute toxic encephalopa-thy is made hoth by ruling out other cominon causes of acute mental status change， and by obtaining a history of exposure to a known central neurotoxin with appropriate dose and duration of exposure in relation to the patient's presentation. For example， a solvent-based spray painter who has been working unusual amounts of overtime without respiratory protection， and who became confused at work， might be suspected of having suffered solvent-induced encephalopathy. A bridge-repair work-er who presents with new onset of cerebellar ataxia after several weeks of sandblasting lead paint without a respirator might be suspected of having lead encephalopathy. Sometimes (but less frequently) focal|删除1换行|neurologic abnormalities， or seizures， are part of the presentation. Additional symptoms and signs are nausea and vomiting (froin loxin effect on the central chemosensory trigger zone)， severe headache，and stiff neck， with absent Brudzinski's and Kernig's signs. These dramatic symptoms are seen with industrial accidents or the mishandling of materials. The additional symptoms of fever and chills would suggest bacterial or viral meningitis. In toxic encephalopathy， CSF examination is usually normal， while in viral disease meningitis， the CSF shows nor-mal sugar values， a low number of cells， or lymphocytosis.**

【55】**Ifinformation about obvious acute chemical exposure does not exist， the differential diagnosis includes many other etiologies， including metabolic encephalopathy due to complications of systemic disease (e.g. hyponatremia， uremia)， medicine or drug ingestion， and viral diseases， the most common heing herpes simplex and equine encephalitis.**

【56】**Chronic Exposure**

【57】**The more subtle and dynamic changes associated with chronic (contin-uous or intcrmittent) exposure are of equal concern， but are less obvi-ous than acute responses. Given an absence of obvious physical disease or other neurological impairment， subclinical encephalopathy is sug-gested by changes in behavioral， affective， social， and vocational perfor-mance that are consistent with exposure to a neurotoxic agent. Subtle neuropsychological deficits， depending on the type of exposure， may first be seen in attention and organizational functions， but also may include visuospatial functioning， motor coordination and speed， verbal fluency， and memory.**

【58】**Chronicity may refer either to ongoing exposure with ongoing mild encephalopathy， or an irreversible encephalopathy caused by a past (or continuing) exposure. In either case， the diagnosis may be difficult. Knowledge of the neurotoxic polential of the substance to which the patient is exposed and the conditions of exposure can be helpful in determining the likelihood of a significant exposure. Thus vocational history is critically important. Jobs or hobbies involving spray painting， metal smelting or reclaiming， welding and cutting， uncontrolled degreasing， dry cleaning， and fabric coating can cause acrosolization or evaporation of large volumes of solvents and metals that can lead to sig-nificant inhalation exposures for the unprolected worker.**

**A. typical pattern of workplace encephalopathic symptoms has its onset after the beginning of expostire at work， and initially will improve on weekends and vacations. The earliest manifestations may be more|删除1换行|apparent to family or friends than to the patient， and may be reported as changes in mood or mental efficiency. In the older patient， attention must be paid to differentiation from the earliest manifestations of com~mon chronic dementias. In practice， if the neurologic exam and neu-ropsychiatric testing do not identify a distinctive disease-related pattern， observation of the course of disease after removal from exposure may provide a convincing differentiation of chronic toxic encephalopathy from Alzheimer’s disease or other age-related neurodegenerative dis~eases. It is important to recogmize that common occupational exposures do not usually cause a focal neurologic presentation suggestive of classi-cal dementia such as aphasia or agnosia. Solvents are among the most widely studied of the groups of occupational neurotoxins. A staging sys-tem  has been developed for solvent exposure that is a model for the study of other toxins that cause encephalopathic changes. **

【60】**FOCAL vs DIFFUSE DEFICIT PATTERNS**

【61】**The general clinical rule has been that toxic encephalopathies are dif fuse rather than focal， reflecting the view that toxic substances influ-ence the brain as a whole. However， we are coming to appreciate that diffuse brain diseases do not affect all structures equally， and focal injury without diffuse repercussions is rare . Diffuse injury is most commonly related to anoxia， disease (degenerative， metabolic， or nutritional)， hypertension， infection， intoxication (alcohol， drug reactions， and toxic substance exposures)， and closed head injuries of the acceleration/deceleration type. Thus focal encephalopathies are generally not attributed to toxins， especially solvents.**

【62】**Focal ncurological or neurobehavioral insults usually present an asymmetrical symptom pattern  and are more likely due to trauma， localized infections， cerebrovascular accidents， or space-displacing lesions (blood vessel malformations or tumors). However， some systemic conditions may affect discrete brain structures and pre-sent a predominantly focal picture， such as severe thiamine deficiency. In general， if a specific cognitive function (or cluster of related functions) is impaired while other functions remain intact， and alertness， orienta-tion， response rate， and learning ability (either verbal or non-verbal) are relatively unaffected， the disorder is more likely to be focal . 【19】**Paraneoplastic Syndromes**

【20】**These result from the indirect effect of the tumor or its metastases and are remote symptom complexes. It is suspected that they are caused by an autoimmune mechanism. The neurological syndromes (cerebral， cere-bellar， spinal cord， peripheral neuropathies， and autonomic) are associ-ated with lung， ovarian， renal， breast， and gastrointestinal cancer， lym-phoma， and Hodgkin’s disease. Cardiovascular syndromes tend to result from cutaneous， urogenital， metabolic， and gastrointestinal cancers. Of those syndromes most relevant to the therapist， peripheral neuropathies are the most common and present in the usual way， with atrophy， weak-ness， areflexia， hypoesthesia or anesthesia， parasthesia， proprioception loss， and paralysis.**

【21】**Neurological Syndromes**

【22】**Cerebral syndromesare mainly associated with lung cancer and Hodgkin’s disease， with the patient suffering dementia， cranial nerve deficits， seizures， depression， motor poliomyelitis， optic neuritis with bi-lateral scotomas， and decreased acuity.**

【23】**Cerebellar paraneoplastic syndromes are mainly caused by lung， cervix， ovary， prostate， and colorectal cancer. The syndrome includes bi-lateral ataxia， nystagmus， dysarthria， and dementia.**

【24】**Spinal cord syndromes should not be a problem for the orthopedic therapist because they involve rapid and progressive upper and lower motor neuron and sensory affects. Lung and renal cancer and lymphoma cause them.**

【25】**Peripheral neuropathies are the most common neurological paraneo-plastic syndromes and the ones most likely to get through to the ortho-pedic therapist because they most mimic orthopedic conditions with neurological involvement. They are associated with breast， lung， gas-trointestinal， and thoracic cancers and lymphoma. Paresthesia， pain， are-flexia， atrophy， weakness， proprioccption and sensory loss， and paraly-sis may all be part of the syndrome.**

【26】**Autonomic Neuropathies**

【27】**These are caused by small cell lung carcinoma. Axonal and neuronal degeneration occurs and presents with orthostatic hypotension， neuro-genic bladder， and altered peristalsis.**

【28】**Neuromuscular Syndromes**

【29】**These cause myasthenia gravis or similar diseases. They are associated with thymoma and cause weakness and excessive fatigability， although one condition (Eaton-Lambert syndrome) actually caused the patient’s strength to increase with repeated testing. Because the hip and thigh muscles are weak and the areas are painful， the patient may end up in the therapist’s office.**

【30】**Other Syndromes**

【31】**These include cardiovascular， cutaneous， urologic， reproductive， gas-trointestinal， and metabolic diseases.**

【32】**Bone Metastases**

【33】**Pathology Almost all malignant cancers have the potential for metas-tasizing to bone， with 50% to 80% of breast， lung， kidney， prostate， gas-trointestinal， and thyroid cancers producing metastases. These metas-tases are usually not life-threatening unless they affect the upper cervical spine， but they are painful and liable to allow fractures to occur as a re-sult of what would otherwise be nonthreatening stresses. The incidence of bone metastasis has increased as improved therapy has increased sur-vival rates in cancer patients. Pain is often caused by pathological frac-tures， but joint pain and direct bone pain from the presence of the tu-mor are also factors. Purely osteoblastic lesions may be asymptomatic until fracturing occurs.**

【34】**Clinical Presentation A metastasis may be the first symptom of can-cer， predating signs or symptoms from the primary tumor. Swelling may be seen if the joint is superficial or the patient is thin； there is usually point tenderness， decreased ROM (Range of Motion)， spasm， painful weakness， parasthesia， and paresis if the fracture affects neurological tissue， and this can include spinal cord signs and symptoms. The pain is generally related to increased activity but is also relentless in nature， being present at rest and frequently worse at night. The effects of a para-neoplastic syndrome may be perceived and/or systemic effects such as weight loss， fever， malaise， and so forth may be present.**

【40】**Management**

【41】**Peripheral fractures are treated with rest； internal and external fixation with immobilization times 2 or 3 times longer than are conventional be-cause of the slowness of bone healing when radiation therapy is being administered. Periarticular fractures are generally treated by joint re-placement. Impending fractures (more than 50% cortex destruction or cortical lesions larger than 2.5 cm or l inch) may be fixed for prophy-laxis. Spinal compression fractures are stable but painful and do not re-quire surgical intervention. Cervical fractures are frequently unstable and， if so， require surgery.**

【42】**Skull Base Metastases Pain precedes neurological signs by weeks. Plain radiographs are usually useless， with MRI and CT scans being more helpful.**

【43】**Jugular Foramen Syndrome This is marked by occipital pain with ref-erence to the vertex and the ipsilateral shoulder and arm. Head move-ment reproduces pain， and there is occipital tenderness over the occip-ital condyle. There is variable cranial nerve (those that exit through the occiput) involvement， which may include dysphonia， dysarthria， dys-phasia， neck rotation and shoulder elevation weakness， ptosis， and Horner’s syndrome.**

【44】**Clivus Metastasis The symptom is vertex headache increased with neck flexion. Cranial nerves 6 through 12 are involved. Initially the signs and symptoms are felt and observed unilaterally， but they progress to be-come bilateral.**

【45】**Sphenoid Sinus Bifrontal headaches with radiation to both to tempo-ral regions and intermittent retro-orbital pain are experienced. There is often nasal stuffiness and fullness of the head， associated with diplopia and bilateral sixth cranial nerve palsy.**

【46】**Vertebral Body Pain is early and precedes neurological signs， and if the cause is not detected early， irreversible neurological deficits such as paraplegia or quadriplegia may develop. In more than 85% of cord com-pression patients， metastases are present， and in 10% of patients with cord compression the only complaint was of pain.**

【47】**Dens Fracture Pain results from the fracture itself and/or the second-ary subluxation. There is often resultant cord or brainstem compression. The pain is felt to radiate over the occiput and into the vertex， and is exacerbated by neck flexion. Progressive sensory and motor signs are found initially in the upper limbs and are associated with autonomic changes. Manipulation and mobilization are extremely dangerous. MRI is the most useful imaging technique.**

【48】**C7-T1 Metastases This is a common site for lung and breast cancer and lymphoma. The spread may be via the vascular system or more di-rectly from involvement of the brachial plexus or the paravertebral space. The pain is usually localized to the adjacent paraspinal region and is characteristically a dull aching， constant pain radiating bilaterally to both shoulders. Percussion tenderness is generally present over the spinous process of the involved vertebra. If there is nerve root compression， there is radicular pain， usually unilaterally， in the C7， C8， and T1 distribu-tions. Neurological findings include numbness and paresthesia in these distributions with weakness of the intrinsic muscles， triceps， and wrist flexors. Horner’s syndrome may be present if the paraspinal ganglion has been affected. CT scanning is the best imaging technique.**

【49】**Lumbar Metastases This mainly affects L1. The symptom is usually a dull， aching midback pain radiating to the SI area and iliac crest that may be unilateral or bilateral. That the pain is exacerbated by lying or sitting and relieved by standing is characteristic. Movement increases the pain， particularly movement from lying to standing. L1 or L2 mo-lor or sensory palsy should always make the therapist concerned be-cause disk lesions at these levels are rare.**

【50】**Sacral Metastases Aching pain felt in the sacrum， coccyx，and/or low back is characteristic. The pain is worsened by lying or sitting and re-lieved by walking. There may be neurological signs， which include perianal sensory deficit and bowel， bladder， and genital dysfunction. The greater sciatic notch area may be tender， and there may be sciatic radic-ular pain if there is compression of the nerve. CT scanning is the im-aging technique of choice.**

【51】**Neurological Metastases**

【52】**Tumor infiltration and sudden or progressive compression caused by pathological fractures give rise to the signs and symptoms， The tissues affected include the peripheral nerve， root， plexus， spinal cord， and meninges， and the pain can be somatic or radicular.**

【53】**Peripheral Nerve Typically， the patient complains of constant causal-gia， dysesthesia， and hypoesthesia. There is commonly radicular pain.**

【54】**The most common area affected is the intercostal nerve from infiltra-tion by a rib tumor. CT scanning images the condition best.**

【55】**Brachial Plexus The lower plexus is the most common site (C7-T1)， although breast cancer and lymphoma may well involve the C5-6 roots. Pain pattems will vary with the levels involved and may reach paraspinally down to the T4 region from the upper plexus and infra-scapularly from the lower. Pain typically precedes motor signs， and these precede sensory ones. Spread along the nerve root to the cord is com-mon， and 50% of these patients will eventually present cord signs and symptoms. Horner’s syndrome may be present. CT scan is the best im-aging technique.**

【56】**Lumbosacral Plexus The most common infiltration occurs from gy-necologic， genitourinary， and colon cancers. Pain was the presenting symptom in 90% of these patients； with weakness， in 60%，second； and numbness in 40%. Two types of pain are typical： local pain in the sacrum， SI joint， low back， or groin， and radicular pain in the lateral， anterior， and posterior leg. CT scanning is the best imaging technique， although MRI has not been fully evaluated for its sensitivity.**

【57】**Leptomeningeal This is infiltration of the cerebrospinal fluid with or without neurological invasion. About 40% of these patients present with pain of one or two types—constant headaches with or without neck stiff-ness or low back and buttock pain. The pain results from traction on the tumor-infiltrated nerves and meninges. Lumbar puncture demonstrates the CSF changes， and myelography images the nodes on the nerves. Mul-tilevel neurological signs and symptoms strongly suggest this condition.**

【58】**Epidural Cord Compression Severe neck and back pain， which oc-curs from either local bone or root compression， is characteristic and is the presenting symptom in 95% of these patients. The pain is of two types：**

【59】**1\. Local pain over the involved vertebral body or radicular pain in the root， distributed unilaterally in the cervical and lumbar regions， bilaterally in the thoracic spine.**

【60】**2\. Neurological symptoms that will vary with the level of the lesion；85% of patients with neurological signs have accompanying vertebral body lesions.**

【61】**Multiple Myeloma**

【62】**This condition composes 14.5% of all hematologic malignancies and1.1% of all malignancies-4.6/100，000 males and 3.1/100，000 in fe-males with 3.5 and 2.4 deaths per 100，000， respectively.**

【63】**Pathology This is a plasma cell carcinoma (PCN) or plasma cell dyscra-sia (PCD) that has multiple foci and mainly affects the bone， bone mar-row， and extraosseous sites. The proliferation of monoclonal plasma cells results in osteclastic activity and consequent fractures and bone pain.**

【1】Because cellulitis of the calf can mimic thrombophlebitis， the two conditions must be differentiated. In cellulitis， the pain is described as being on the surface， no palpable cord is present， and Homans’ sign is absent. Careful examination reveals that pain is induced by light palpation rather than deep palpation over the course of the vein. Likewise， the area of erythema is more clearly demarcated， occasionally with an associated open wound. An inflated sphygmomanometer requires high pressure to reproduce the pain of cellulitis， and often there is no difference in pressure between the two calves. These findings contrast with those reported in patients with thrombophlebitis. Because thrombophlebitis may coexist with a popliteal (Baker's) cyst， venous Doppler ultrasonography should be performed in all patients with popliteal cysts.

【2】**Other Conditions**

If the diagnosis is still unclear after a complete physical examination|删除1换行|is conducted with special attention to the musculoskeletal， vascular， and nervous systems， noninvasive and invasive studies of the vascular system， electromyography， CT， MRI， and occasionally myelography may be helpful.

【4】**Less common diagnostic considerations**

【5】Sudden onset of pain in the leg， especially the lower leg and sometimes associated with paralysis， paresthesia， pallor， or absence of arterial pulsation， suggests acute arterial embolism. The likelihood of this diagnosis is increased by the presence of atrial fibrillation. Vague arthralgias and muscle aches are often seen with viral and flulike infections， but no joint abnormality can be detected on physical examination in these cases. Primary bone tumors are rare in adults； however， pain from metastatic bone disease is frequently seen in patients with breast， lung， and prostatic tumors.

【6】_Chondromalacia patellae (anterior knee pain syndrome)， though more_ common in adolescents than adults， may be seen in patients in their40s and 50s. These patients characteristically have pain， stiffness， grating， or locking of the knee. The pain is worse when the knee is weight bearing in flexion. Crepitation and pain with manipulation of the patella over the femoral condyle are characteristic. Pain is exacerbated when the patient tenses the quadriceps with the knee in free extension while the examiner is depressing the upper pole of the patella.

【7】Meralgia paresthetica， which is slightly more common in men than women， is caused by entrapment of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve by the tensor fasciae latae. The patient complains of pain， burning， or tingling over the lateral aspect of the thigh that is occasionally worse at night or after exercise. It is alleviated by rest， particularly in the sitting position.

Peripheral neuropathy is more common in diabetic patients but may be seen in others. Patients complain of burning，tingling， and numbness， particularly in the feet. They may have a sensation of coldness， but no decrease in vascular pulsations is noted in those with pure peripheral neuropathy. Diabetic patients with peripheral neuropathy often have associated vascular insufficiency.Physical|删除1换行|findings include sensory loss (often symmetrical)， muscle wasting， weakness， decreased tendon reflexes， and signs of arterial insufficiency.

Obturator hernias， an uncommon cause of pain， occur more frequently in elderly debilitated women than in other patients. The female-to-male ratio is 6：1. Patients usually present with pain along the anteromedial aspect of the thigh. This pain is increased by adduction of the thigh. Pain may also be felt in the hip or knee. The pain may be associated with intermittent bouts of nausea， vomiting， abdominal pain， and distention， all signs of small bowel obstruction. Obturator hernias should be given particular consideration in|删除1换行|elderly women who complain of pain in the hip or knee with no|删除换行|objective evidence of DJD or other common causes.**

【10】Iliopsoas bursitis， a rare condition， should be suspected if the patient has gradual onset of groin pain that is exacerbated by flexion or internal rotation of the hip.

【11】Half of the patients with pseudothrombophlebitis due to a popliteal(Baker's) cyst have rheumatoid arthritis. In one study of patients with a confirmed popliteal cyst， only 50% had palpable masses and 12%had masses below the popliteal space. Baker's cyst should be suspected in all patients with thrombophlebitis and rheumatoid arthritis and in all patients with suspected thrombophlebitis but no venographic evidence of phlebitis. An arthrogram is essential to the diagnosis of a popliteal cyst. Ultrasonography may help the physician diagnose an intact cyst， but it is often not useful in the diagnosis of a ruptured popliteal cyst.

Rheumatoid arthritis is a relatively uncommon cause of pain in the lower extremity. The joint pain usually lasts for a few weeks， with characteristic morning stiffness， joint tenderness， and pain with motion. The patient frequently has joint effusion， soft tissue swelling， and synovial thickening. In this clinical scenario， a positive cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody along with a positive rheumatoid factor makes the diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis highly probable. Pseudothrombophlebitis should be suspected when calf pain occurs in any patient with rheumatoid arthritis， especially if active|删除换行|inflammation of the knee is present.

【13】Spinal stenosis (neurogenic claudication， cauda equina claudication) is often difficult to differentiate from intermittent claudication due to arterial insufficiency. The patient's history is particularly important because the two conditions affect the same age group. Patients with calf pain due to spinal stenosis state that the pain starts insidiously， is exacerbated by walking， and is particularly related to extension of the spine. They may have associated backache or buttock pain， which is relatively uncommon in patients with intermittent claudication. A paresthetic quality to the pain suggests a neurogenic origin. Patients with spinal stenosis do not experience prompt relief of pain with cessation of exercise (as do those with arterial insufficiency)； they feel greater relief when they lie or sit down with their thighs flexed； they also do not have pain while riding a bicycle because the spine is in a flexed position. In any patient who has signs of intermittent claudication and rides a bicycle without difficulty， spinal stenosis should be suspected.

【14】Musculotendinous rupture of the gastrocnemius or plantaris muscle， particularly during athletic activities such as jogging， running， and tennis， is characterized by a sudden onset of pain in the leg (“it felt like I got a shot in the leg"). Frequently， the physician can palpate the retracted end of the plantaris muscle.

【15】Trochanteric bursitis usually manifests as pain over the greater trochanter， in the buttock， and in the lateral thigh along the distribution of the second lumbar dermatome.On physical examination， the patient may be found to limp and usually to have marked point tenderness over the greater trochanter. The differential diagnosis consists of arthritis of the hip or lumbar spine problems. The major factors in differential diagnosis include pain on palpation over the trochanteric bursa and the absence of sensory loss， which would be seen with lumbar disk disease. The pain is not exacerbated by coughing and sneezing but is by squatting， climbing stairs， and sitting with the painful leg crossed over the other one. It is alleviated by infiltration of the trochanteric bursa with local anesthetics， steroids， or both.

【16】Cyclic hip pain that coincides with menstruation suggests endometriosis. The pain is usually unilateral.Other uncommon causes of knee pain are meniscal cysts， bipartite patella， fat pad irritation(Hoffa's syndrome)， and neuromas.

【17】**The leg and sports medicine**

【18】The most common causes of chronic leg pain in runners include shin _splints， stress fractures， and compartment syndromes . Shin_ splints represent musculotendinous inflammation from overuse and probably subclinical periosteal reaction. The pain is either anterolateral or posteromedial along the distal tibia. The painful areas are tender on palpation.

【19】通用删除16(英):<u>FIGURE 24.9Pain in the shin， often seen in runners.</u>

【20】With stress fractures there is usually point tenderness over the involved bone， and the diagnosis may be confirmed radiographically. Stress fractures are more common in experienced long-distance runners， particularly those who attempt to run more than 20-30 miles per week. These fractures may occur in the tibia， fibula， or metatarsus. Lateral knee pain in long-distance runners suggests iliotibial band _friction syndrome._

Compartment syndromes occur when the fascial compartment is too|删除1换行|small to accommodate the approximately 20% increase in muscle size that occurs with strenuous exercise. This results in limited venous outflow and tends to produce ischemic pain of the involved tissue. Patients with compartment syndromes usually present with a gradual onset (over 1 or more years) of bilateral pain that is progressive， dull， aching， and particularly worse after long runs. Paresthesias may also be present. The anterior compartment of the leg is usually affected； the next most likely affected is the posterior compartment， followed by the posterior superficial compartment. Physical findings include tenderness in the muscle mass itself but not as much in the bone and tendons. Elevated compartment pressures are diagnostic.

【42】**Pain in the Lower Extremity and Limping in Children**

【43】The physician should approach leg pain or limp in children as in adults-that is， determine whether it originates in joints or soft tissue. The most common causes of childhood leg pain originating in the soft tissue are unusual or strenuous exercise and trauma. Fractures constitute the most common cause of acute limp in children. Other _common causes of leg pain are growing pains， Legg-Calue-Perthes disease(epiphysitis ofthe hip)， Osgood-Schlatter disease (an abnormality of the_ _epiphyseal ossification of the tibial tubercle)， chondromalacia patellae， and_ _ossification of the Achilles insertion. Limping can be due to pain， weakness，_ or structural abnormality. It is important to determine the duration and progression of the limp， history of trauma， nature of pain， and any weakness and to observe the gait .

(From Sawyer J， Kapoor M. The limping child： a systematic approach to diagnosis. Am Fam Physician. 2009；79：215-224.)</u></u>

【45】**Nature of patient**

【46】If a limp occurs when a young child begins to walk， congenital dislocation of one or both hips should be considered. Toddler’s fracture， an undisplaced fracture of the distal tibia， may occur when weight bearing first occurs (9 months to 3 years). It may manifest as a limp or the inability to bear weight on the affected leg. In 1- to 5-year-old patients， other common causes of limp include toxic synovitis， septic arthritis or osteomyelitis， developmental abnormalities， and juvenile rheumatoid arthritis. In contrast， in 5- to 10-year-old patients， the more common causes are trauma， toxic synovitis， and infectious joint or bone disease. Legg-Calve-Perthes disease (epiphysitis of the hip) usually occurs between ages 5 and 7 years. In patients 10-15 years old， _slipped femoral epiphyses and patellar problems are more common. In_ children between ages 10 and 12， pain in the heel is most often caused _by painful bursitis or irregular ossification of a calcaneal apophysis._

【47】**Nature of symptoms**

【48】Growing pains is a general diagnosis that is being made less frequently as physicians become more expert in making specific diagnoses. However， growing pains do exist， and they are now thought to be a form of myalgia. The aching pain is intermittent and usually located in the leg muscles， particularly in the front of the thigh， the calf， and the back of the knee. Additionally， the pain is deep and localized to areas outside the joints. It is usually bilateral and typically occurs late in the day， although it may awaken the child from a sound sleep. Growing pains may be exacerbated by excessive running during the day， but exercise is not usually a factor. The findings that the pain is nonarticular， bilateral， and usually unrelated to activity are essential to the accurate diagnosis of growing pains. Children with growing pains show no abnormal physical findings.

【49】Most serious diseases that cause leg pain in children (except slipped capital femoral epiphyses) are usually unilateral. It is often associated with a limp， and the pain is occasionally referred to the medial aspect of the knee. 【106】简短段落群删除-1:<u>**T-CELL PROLYMPHOCYTIC LEUKEMIA**</u>

【107】**INTRODUCTION**

T-cell prolymphocytic leukemia (T-PLL) is a rare mature(post-thy mic) T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder that affects adults， occurs more frequently in men， and is characterized by an aggressive clinical course and a poor outcome 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1-11\]</u>. T-PLL is composed of small- to medium-sized lymphocytes with prominent nucleoli. The principal disease characteris-tics are organomegaly (especially splenomegaly and lymph-adenopathy)， anemia， thrombocytopenia， skin lesions， and prominent (often rapidly increasing) lymphocytosis in the blood (often >100×10/L). The median lymphocyte count is 40×10%L 通用删除6(英):<u>\[11，12\]</u>. The skin， liver， and other organs may also be involved 通用删除6(英):<u>\[13，14\]</u>. Skin manifestation includes nod-ules， maculopapular rash， or rarely erythroderma. Peripheral edema， particularly periorbital and/or conjunctival， occurs relatively frequently and seems to be particularly charac-teristic of T-PLL 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10\]</u>. A subset of patients experiences an initial (median： 33 months， range： 6-103 months) indolent clinical course with stable moderate leukocytosis， with subsequent progression to the aggressive stage 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>. There|删除1换行|is no association with human T-cell lymphotropic viruses(HTLV-I/II)通用删除6(英):<u>\[16\]</u>.**

【109】Prior to the use of pentostatin and alemtuzumab in clinical protocols， the outcome for T-PLL patients was exceedingly poor (median survival <1 year). Alemtuzumab (Campath； humanized monoclonal antibody directed against the CD52antigen) is an effective agent in T-PLL and represents a sig-nificant improvement over other types of therapy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[6，9，17，18\]</u>. While the use of alemtuzumab in particular has improved remissions， the disease remains incurable 通用删除6(英):<u>\[5\]</u>. The only potential curative treatment is allogeneic stem cell transplan-tation 通用删除6(英):<u>\[8\]</u>. Best results are achieved if treatment with alemtu-zumab is followed by allogeneic transplant 通用删除6(英):<u>\[6，17\]</u>.

【110】**MORPHOLOGY**

【111】**Blood**

**In the blood film， leukemic cells have scanty basophilic cytoplasm without cytoplasmic granules and prominent nucleolus . In a subset of cases， the nucleolus may be inconspicuous， resembling B-CLL cells. Fifty per-cent cases have round or oval nuclei and the remaining cases|删除1换行|have irregular nuclei， often with convolution (cerebriform)， although less prominent than seen in Sezary or adult T-cell lymphoma/leukemia (ATLL； flower) cells.

【113】**Bone Marrow**

【114】Bone marrow (BM) involvement  is character-ized by prominent interstitial lymphoid infiltrate， but it may be subtle， nodular， and even diffuse. Reticulin fibrosis is increased.

【115】**Lymph Nodes**

【116】**T-PLL involvement of the lymph node is usually paracorti-cal with preserved follicles and patent sinusoids， but may be diffuse with total effacement of lymph node architecture. Leukemic cells are medium sized with nucle-oli， but small cell infiltrate without prominent nucleoli (remi-niscent of CLL) may also be present in the subset of T-PLL cases.**

【117】**Spleen**

【118】The spleen shows dense white and red pulp infiltration and dense lymphoid infiltration in both portal areas and within sinusoids and cords .

【200】**Renal Cell Carcinoma， Papillary Type**

【201】**Clinical Features**

【202】Comprises about 10% to 15% of all RCCs； mostly sporadic， less than 5% associated with hereditary PRCC syndrome that involves the c-met gene on chromosome 7q31

【203】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Signs and symptoms similar to clear cell RCC More likely to be bilateral or multiple than other RCCs</u>

【204】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Significantly better outcome than that of the clear cell type</u>

【205】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Gross Pathology</u>

【206】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Solitary， well-circumscribed cortical mass</u>

【207】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Fibrous pseudocapsule</u>

【208】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Necrosis and hemorrhage common</u>

【209】简短段落群删除-1:<u>More likely to be bilateral or multifocal than other RCCs</u>

【210】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Histopathology</u>

【211】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Papillae and tubulopapillary structures with true fibrovascular cores</u>

【212】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Solid pattern due to tightly compact growth of papillae</u>

【213】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Foamy histiocytes expanding papillary core characteristic</u>

【214】**Psammoma bodies common**

【215】通用删除16(英):<u>Figure 10-28. Renal cell carcinoma， papillary type. Papillae and tubulopapillary structures with true fibrovascular cores. Foamy histiocytes expanding papillary core are characteristic.</u>

【216】Subdivided into two types based on morphology

【217】简短段落群删除-1:<u>\- Type l： papillae lined with single layer of cells， usually low-grade nuclear features， and scant cytoplasm</u>

【218】简短段落群删除-1:<u>_—_ Type 2： pseudostratified nuclei of higher nuclear grade and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm</u>

【219】简短段落群删除-1:<u>**Sarcomatoid differentiation in 5% cases**</u>

【220】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry</u>

【221】简短段落群删除-1:<u>**Pan-cytokeratin and low-molecular-weight cytokeratin positive**</u>

【222】简短段落群删除-1:<u>CK7 positive in 80% of type I cases and 20% type II cases</u>

【223】简短段落群删除-1:<u>EMA and vimentin positive in 50% of cases</u>

【224】简短段落群删除-1:<u>CD10 and RCC antigen positive in most cases</u>

【225】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Other Techniques for Diagnosis</u>

【226】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Cytogenetics： trisomy or tetrasomy 7 and 17 and loss of Y chromosome are the most common cytogenetic changes</u>

【228】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Papillary adenoma</u>

【229】简短段落群删除-1:<u>FBy WHO criteria， smaller than 5 mm and low nuclear grade (Fuhrman nuclear grade l or 2)</u>

【230】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Metanephric adenoma</u>

【231】简短段落群删除-1:<u>**Sharp circumscription from the kidney parenchyma without capsule**</u>

【232】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Tightly packed tumor cells form small acini，</u>

【233】简短段落群删除-1:<u>tubulopapillary structures</u>

【234】简短段落群删除-1:<u>TTumor cells with scant cytoplasm， uniform nuclei without mitosis or nucleoli</u>

【235】简短段落群删除-1:<u>CK7 negative， but WT-1 positive</u>

【237】简短段落群删除-1:<u>Has a tumor capsule and may show a distinct triphasic pattern with blastemal， stromal， and epithelial components after careful sampling</u>

【21】Alternative distributions that may affect portions of one lobe or involve more than one lobe of the brain include classic vascular territory lesions of the cerebral cortex and subcortical regions. For example, middle cerebral artery territory deficits which include subcortical regions classically produce contralateral deficits of arm and face more than leg, and contralateral sensory loss with increased reflexes. If originating in the dominant hemisphere, aphasia will be apparent. Other findings include apraxia, contralateral field deficits, and early on there may be gaze deviations to the side of the lesion. Anterior cerebral artery territory lesions cause deficits of contralateral leg more than arm and face. There may be contralateral cortical sensory loss in the leg, and increased deep tendon reflexes . Additionally, incontinence and frontal lobe signs may be present. Posterior cerebral artery territory deficits may produce a homonymous hemianopia, contralateral sensory loss, and sometimes visual agnosia or alexia without agraphia. Borderzone vascular territory syndromes termed watershed syndromes, such as the bilateral anterior watershed territory (man in a barrel syndrome) ischemic syndromes, can be particularly challenging to identify.

【22】##### Subcortical white matter disturbances

【23】Consolidation of pyramidal tract fibers makes it feasible that even small lesions can produce substantial deficits . While affectation of the corona radiata may elicit more variability in degree of paresis among face, arm, and leg, lesions of the posterior limb of the internal capsule may produce a uniform deficit throughout the contralateral side. Sufficiently large subcortical lesions often produce visual field deficits.
